title: Tenant-shard-aware coalescer for multi-backend trace export
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Problem: High-cardinality tenant traffic causes inefficient fan-out when we mirror spans to multiple tracing backends (Tempo/Jaeger/OTLP collectors). Small bursts from many tenants create lots of tiny requests, increasing per-request overhead and burst-backed queueing in destination endpoints. We also see duplicated span payloads across backends and an increased likelihood of transient backend failures causing dropped traces for a subset of tenants.

Goal: Implement a tenant-shard-aware coalescer and dispatch layer in the trace export path that reduces per-span overhead, applies backpressure and circuit-breaking per backend, and preserves trace fidelity (trace IDs, parent-child relationships, timestamps). The coalescer should batch spans by tenant shard and short time window, coalesce identical metadata and resource attributes, and support conditional fanout to multiple backends with per-backend policy decisions (retry budgets, sample rate overrides).

Non-goals: This ticket does not change sampling logic for application-level SDKs, and does not migrate legacy Jaeger tag formats. Those are separate follow-ups.

Requirements and success criteria:
- Reduce number of outbound HTTP/gRPC requests to each tracing backend by >= 40% for steady-state tenant traffic (measured on staging trace load).
- Maintain P95 trace latency representation within 5% of baseline (no perceptible distortion of critical path timings).
- End-to-end tests that verify trace assembly across coalesced batches preserves span ordering and parent-child relationships for reconstruction in Tempo and Jaeger.
- Metrics: per-tenant outbound-request-rate, coalesce-ratio, per-backend circuit-breaker state, retry-budget-consumption, dropped-spans-by-reason.

Design summary:
1) Tenant sharding: use our existing tenant_id -> shard mapping to keep grouping predictable and cache-friendly. Shard size tuned to balance latency and batch efficiency.
2) Short-window coalescing: hold incoming spans for up to 50ms (configurable) or until size limit reached, then emit a single batch per shard per backend.
3) Attribute de-duplication: collapse identical resource and instrumentation library attributes into shared batch-level metadata to cut payload size.
4) Multi-backend fanout: compute per-backend decision for each batch (send/drop/route-to-fallback) based on backend health, configured sampling overrides, and tenant policy. Maintain separate time-series for each backend.
5) Backpressure and circuit-breaking: per-backend token buckets + adaptive circuit-breaker that trips on elevated 5xx/timeout rates and uses exponential backoff with jitter. While open, attempt a thin-retry to fallback backend or NACK to upstream with metrics.
6) Observability: expose internal traces for the coalescer itself (span per batch lifecycle), and expose metrics and events to Console for rollouts.
7) Compatibility: keep OTLP payload shapes intact for direct passthrough when coalescing disabled. Ensure Jaeger legacy fields are preserved when routing to Jaeger-compatible sinks.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (Spike, 1 week): microbenchmark coalescing logic in a sandbox; measure batch-size vs latency tradeoffs on recorded staging traffic.
- M2 (Core impl, 2 weeks): implement coalescer module with tenant-shard grouping, attribute dedupe, and simple fanout to a single backend. Unit tests for ordering and metadata preservation.
- M3 (Resilience, 1 week): add per-backend circuit-breaker and token bucket backpressure. Integrate with retry budgets and fallback routing.
- M4 (Multi-backend & telemetry, 1 week): wire up parallel dispatch to Tempo/Jaeger/OTLP, add internal tracing and metrics.
- M5 (Canary, 1 week): rollout behind feature flag for small tenant cohort, monitor metrics and rollback criteria.
- M6 (Gradual ramp, 1 week): expand to broader cohort and finalize config knobs for production.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: batch ordering, attribute dedupe, per-backend decision logic.
- Integration tests: end-to-end trace reconstruction between coalesced batches and Tempo/Jaeger backends using a synthetic trace generator.
- Load test: replay captured production-ish trace traffic into staging; measure reduce-in-requests and end-to-end latency distortion.
- Chaos scenarios: simulate backend timeouts and 5xx to validate circuit-breakers and fallback paths.

Rollout and monitoring playbook:
- Feature flag gated. Canary with 2% of tenants for 48 hours, then 10% for 24 hours if metrics stable.
- Key dashboards: coalesce_ratio, outbound_request_rate_per_backend, circuit_breaker_open_count, retry_budget_consumption, dropped_spans_by_reason, reconstructed_trace_fidelity_score (synthetic).
- Rollback triggers: >10% increase in reconstructed_trace_error, >5% regression in P95 trace latency, or backend error rate increases beyond thresholds attributable to new path.

Security and compliance:
- Coalescer runs within existing trace pipeline trust boundary; does not introduce new plaintext storage. All in-flight aggregation happens in-memory while respecting tenant isolation.
- Feature requires SRE security review prior to broad rollout (flagged below).

Open questions and trade-offs:
- Window size: 50ms provides good batching for most workloads but may hurt ultra-low-latency traces. We'll expose config per-tenant-class.
- Shard granularity: larger shards increase batching but can delay a single-tenant burst. Consider hybrid strategy for high-volume tenants.
- Payload dedupe vs CPU cost: dedupe reduces egress bytes but adds CPU; cost trade-off will be evaluated in M1.

Acceptance criteria checklist (to mark as Done):
- [ ] Coalescer landed in mainline code with feature flag and config.
- [ ] Integration and load tests passing in CI.
- [ ] Canary run completed and metrics meet success criteria.
- [ ] Console dashboards added and SLO alerts configured.
- [ ] Security review completed and signed off.

updates: 2025-02-13: Spike started. Captured 1 hour of prod-like trace traffic to replay in sandbox. Observed mean per-span payload ~1.4KB; grouping by tenant with 50ms window reduced requests by ~52% in prototype.
2025-02-20: Core coalescer implemented (initial PR opened). Tests added for ordering and attribute dedupe. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-pipeline/pull/4123
2025-02-25: Feedback from infra review: make shard map pluggable and add metrics for batch-size distribution. Added perf budget checks to CI.
2025-03-01: Circuit-breaker implementation completed. Verified fallback routing to secondary OTLP endpoint during simulated primary backend failure. Added unit tests for backpressure behavior.

2025-03-03: Canary flag enabled for internal QA tenants. Early metrics: coalesce_ratio=0.47, outbound_reqs_down=45%, no regression in P95 latency observed. Scheduling SRE security review for 2025-03-05.
